answer:
The video game you're referring to is **"NFL Football"** (released in 1989), which was named after the National Football League (the sports association that chooses where the Super Bowl is held). It was developed/published by **LJN** for the **Nintendo Entertainment System (NES)**.

Nintendo's limit on games per developer/publisher per year on that platform was **5 games**. This policy, often called the "5 game/year rule," was enforced during the NES era to prevent publishers from dominating the marketplace and to manage shelf space. The "NFL Football" title by LJN was included among these eligible releases under this fiscal policy.
